subject: Network stitching: peering vs PrivateLink vs site-to-site VPN — decision + cutover runbook
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@orion-retail.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Ops <infra@avasol.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Connecting Orion private deployment — options and constraints

Hey Michael —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We have a clear requirement to stand up Redwood Private for inference (payment fraud detection) inside our VPCs. Security / compliance requires no public egress from the data plane and we need an operational plan that minimizes blast radius during cutover.

High-level constraints:
- Primary region: us-west-2, with DR in us-east-1.
- Traffic volume: ~120 requests/sec peak, median request latency requirement < 120ms (app <200ms end-to-end).
- No cross-tenant routing in our VPCs; we can accept a managed interface endpoint if it preserves IAM policies + flow logs.

Can you sketch tradeoffs between: VPC peering, PrivateLink (AWS VPC Endpoint Services), and site-to-site VPN (IPsec) for this deployment? Also want a short cutover runbook + rollback triggers.

Jared
Senior Cloud Architect, Orion Retail

Attachments: none
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@orion-retail.com>, Ava Ops <infra@avasol.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connecting Orion private deployment — options and constraints

Jared — thanks for the clear constraints. I did a quick assessment and attached a one-page decision matrix (net-stitching-matrix-v1.pdf) and a cost sketch. Summary up-front:

Short answer (tl;dr):
- PrivateLink (interface endpoint) gives the strongest isolation & per-service IAM controls, predictable permission model, and easiest auditability (flow logs/AWS PrivateLink logs). Latency overhead is usually small (5-25ms) depending on AZ mapping. Operationally the path is easiest for RBAC and per-account connection.
- VPC Peering: low latency (virtually no additional hop), cheaper for sustained cross-account high-throughput, but scales poorly for multi-account topologies and lacks a straightforward per-service policy — peering also requires route table management and can open up more surface area if not carefully restricted.
- Site-to-Site VPN (IPsec): useful when you cannot add endpoints (e.g., on-prem segments) and provides strong encryption in transit but adds variable latency (20-100ms typical) and operational overhead for tunnels, BGP, and failover. Generally worst for low-latency production inference unless you have direct SD-WAN/MPLS underlay.

Decision pointers by requirement:
- For ORION's requirement (no public egress + compliance + per-service audit): PrivateLink > VPC Peering > S2S VPN.
- For lowest per-token cost at high sustained throughput (if you were moving many TB of tokens across accounts): VPC Peering might win.
- If you need cross-region DR with minimal ops: use PrivateLink in each region and control routing at the application layer; peering across regions is not supported (unless inter-region peering) and will add complexity.

I've attached a cutover checklist (cutover-checklist.md) with rollback triggers. High level runbook below — please review with infra and compliance.

---
Cutover plan (PrivateLink preferred) — high level:
1) Provision NLB-backed service in Redwood Private control plane (internal service ENIs per AZ).
2) Create AWS Network Load Balancer in us-west-2 and register backend targets in isolated subnet.
3) Provide your account with our service name (com.amazonaws.vpce-svc-...).
4) You create Interface VPC Endpoint(s) in your VPC (one per AZ where app runs). Do NOT enable DNS integration until testing passes.
5) Testing phase (non-prod):
   - Create ephemeral endpoint in staging VPC, point a staging workload at it, validate TLS; measure p95 latencies and request success rates.
   - Exchange flow logs and PrivateLink metrics.
6) Cut traffic to new endpoint in prod during low-traffic window. Keep original path (peering/VPN) in place for 24 hours as failback.
7) Monitor: p95 latency, error rate, CPU on GPU nodes, and anomalous auth failures. Rollback triggers: p95 latency > 180ms sustained for 5min OR error rate > 2% for 5min OR a TLS negotiation failure spike.

Approx cost sketch (monthly, us-west-2):
- PrivateLink: endpoint-hours + data processing — expecting ~$1.2k–$2.5k depending on throughput (rough).
- VPC Peering: small one-time route configuration + nominal hourly cost, data egress pricing varies by account.
- VPN: appliance cost + hourly tunnel + egress; could be $3k+/mo depending on throughput.

I'll loop in Kimberly on security implications and Neha for operational readiness. If you prefer a quick call, we can run the testing checklist with your infra team this week.

—Michael
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference

Attachments: net-stitching-matrix-v1.pdf, stitching-cost-estimates-2025-07-14.xlsx, cutover-checklist.md
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Jared Cole <jared.cole@orion-retail.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jul 2025 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connecting Orion private deployment — options and constraints

Jared / team — a couple of security notes to call out before you decide:

- PrivateLink: very nice for least-privilege from an AWS network model perspective. Ensure endpoint policy restricts which principals can attach and which operations are allowed. We'll propose a Managed Endpoint Policy and share templates.
- VPC Peering: you must lock down route tables and SGs carefully — peering flattens the L3 topology and can inadvertently expose management subnets. Peering also complicates flow logging centralization because flows appear as intra-VPC traffic.
- VPN: if chosen, prefer a dedicated crypto profile and hardware-backed HSM on our side for key management; document rekey windows and alerts.

Operational monitoring / auditability:
- Enable VPC Flow Logs for endpoints and our NLB. Set up a daily digest to compliance mailbox.
- Add a synthetic probe from your app subnets against the endpoint URL and alert on 5m p95 > 150ms.

Compliance ask: please capture expected retention window for flow logs — we recommend 90 days for initial audit. If you need longer retention we can discuss archival to your S3.

Kimberly
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@orion-retail.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Ava Ops <infra@avasol.com>, LatticeCloud (solutions@latticecloud.io)
Date: Wed, 16 Jul 2025 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Connecting Orion private deployment — options and constraints

Quick synthesis and requested next steps —

We recommend proceeding with PrivateLink for initial production cutover given Orion's compliance requirement (no public egress) and need for per-service auditability. Action items:

- Jared / Orion: please provision a staging VPC with one AZ and let us know the account-id and staging subnet CIDRs by Thursday 7/17.
- Orion infra (Ava Ops): create a staging interface endpoint per our NLB service name; keep DNS disabled until we validate.
- Neha: prepare a blue/green traffic-swap plan and data-plane throttling knobs; share the rate-limiter playbook.
- Kimberly: provide endpoint policy template + recommended retention window (we suggested 90 days).
- Michael: I will schedule a 60-minute cutover dry-run with infra and support (proposed 7/21 10:00am PT).

If you want to optimize cost later and you find throughput is extremely high, we can revisit peering for a high-volume backbone between accounts. For now, we value minimal blast radius and auditability.

Please reply-all with sign-off or objections. If no objections by EOD 7/17 we'll lock the dry-run.

—Michael
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
